questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is deciding how to package several daily medications for one patient. Which statements correctly apply the Schedule II/III rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A stable maintenance classification permits a Schedule II drug to share a multi-drug single-dose pouch.
A licensee may not dispense a Schedule II or III controlled substance in a multi-drug single-dose package.
That prohibition does not by its own terms ban a single-drug single-dose package.
Every form of compliance packaging is prohibited for every Schedule II or III controlled substance.
The policy phrase 'unless otherwise prohibited' preserves the regulatory Schedule II/III restriction.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is redesigning one patient's compliance packaging. Assuming all other requirements are satisfied, which proposed placements are not prohibited by 247 CMR 9.08(3)(b)? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Place stable Schedule III buprenorphine in the same multi-drug single-dose pouch as the patient's other morning medications.
Keep Schedule II methylphenidate in a separate single-drug single-dose package rather than the patient's multi-drug pouch.
Place Schedule IV alprazolam in a multi-drug single-dose package after confirming the other packaging requirements.
Place stable Schedule III testosterone in a multi-drug single-dose pouch because maintenance status creates an exception.
Keep Schedule II oxycodone in a separate single-drug single-dose package rather than combining it with other medications.

questions.stem: A patient receives stable Schedule III buprenorphine therapy. The pharmacy proposes to combine each dose in a multi-drug single-dose pouch with the patient's other morning medications. May maintenance status justify that placement?

choices.text: Yes, because a stable maintenance regimen overrides the controlled-substance packaging restriction.
No; Schedule III drugs may not enter a multi-drug single-dose package under 247 CMR 9.08(3)(b).
No, because every controlled substance is prohibited from every form of compliance packaging.
Yes, if the patient signs a written consent to combine the medications.
Yes, if the pharmacy limits the package to a 60-day supply.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist practising collaboratively in a retail drug business is reviewing what the statute permits her to do there. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Patients must be 18 years of age or older in that setting.
She may initiate a new Schedule II therapy whenever the referral identifies the diagnosis.
She may extend current therapy prescribed by the supervising physician by 30 days.
She may modify dosages of any medication the patient is currently taking.
She may administer vaccines under the terms of her agreement.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy proposes to run a walk-in clinic for a newly designated vaccine during a public health event. Which statements about what must be in place are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A practitioner standing prescription alone opens this pathway.
The Commissioner must determine that health care professionals will be insufficient.
A Commissioner order authorizing the administration removes any need for a prescription.
Administration must accord with the Commissioner's order as well as a practitioner instrument.
A designation of the vaccine by the Commissioner is required.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy operating under a Commissioner vaccine order is revising its written protocols. It already covers training and adverse-event response. Which proposed decisions correctly identify additional protocol subjects that 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(b) expressly requires? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Retain procedures for proper storage even when vaccine arrives directly from the distributor.
Add a regulation-mandated written-consent protocol before every administered dose.
Retain procedures for return of vaccine even if unused doses are uncommon.
Add a regulation-mandated rule to report every dose to the immunization registry within 24 hours.
Retain recordkeeping procedures for vaccine administration.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is asked in one shift to administer a long-acting injectable antipsychotic, testosterone for gender-affirming care, and an antibiotic for a sexually transmitted infection. Which statements about the statutory basis for each are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: All three rest on the same statutory clause and share the same conditions.
The antipsychotic route requires the direction of a prescribing practitioner.
The antipsychotic route additionally requires departmental regulations.
The testosterone route rests on a prescription for that purpose.
The sexually transmitted-infection route additionally requires the departmental regulations that govern the mental-health route.

instruction: Solve each item independently from current official authority before reading anything else in the repository. Record your selected choice IDs and your reasoning, then commit the Phase-1 lock. Do not open data/questions/, data/rules/, the authoring report, the post-lock reveal, the generated site payload, the controller ledger, the plan issue or any git history for these questions before that lock is committed.
content_boundary: Contains only question ID, type, stem and choices plus non-substantive package identity metadata. Excludes keyed answers, explanations, choice analysis, rule and drug identifiers, area, topic, subtopic, difficulty, family, provenance and all author reasoning.
